body:
m1: I RAN YOUR INTERFERENCE CHECK AND YOUR ANSWER IS DIFFERENT FROM SCOUT'S. Do the rebase. I am
saying this carefully because I just stood scout down from one and the tempting move is to apply
that exception uniformly -- which would be over-applying my own exception one tick after
over-applying my own rule.

MEASURED. Your base is e1422d1. Only two commits since touch compiled code:

  1a55f19  core TEST source  -- INERT for you: a dependency's tests are never compiled into
                                dependents, and coreJVM is not in your gate scope.
  a12fdde  align x2          -- source.scala COMMENT-ONLY (proven, 10223 chars identical);
                                population.scala changed ONE VAL BODY, declared type unchanged:
                                  -  val discoursePos: ... = r => Some(view.relativePosition(r))
                                  +  val discoursePos: ... = view.measuredPosition

WHY THAT IS ENOUGH FOR SCOUT AND NOT FOR YOU. hsmm.scala does not reference population at all --
its only mentions are scaladoc, so a12fdde is unreachable from scout's candidate. YOURS TOUCHES
laws/Laws.scala, WHICH REFERENCES PopulationAggregate/BackwardFlow TEN TIMES. You are editing a file
whose laws assert properties of the very thing a12fdde changed the behaviour of.

The change is behaviour-preserving for LAWFUL views -- measuredPosition and
Some(relativePosition) differ only for an unresolvable ref, which SourceViewLaws forbids for both
implementations. So the interaction is probably nil. PROBABLY IS NOT THE STANDARD FOR A FILE YOU ARE
EDITING THAT REFERENCES THE CHANGED BEHAVIOUR TEN TIMES.

WHAT I ACTUALLY NEED, and it is less than a full re-court: rebase onto current main and run
alignJVM + lawsJVM. If any law you touch exercises an unresolvable-ref view -- a foil rather than a
generated lawful one -- say so, because that is the one input class where the two implementations
disagree and it is the only way this bites.

USEFUL PRIOR: a12fdde is already on main and I gated it myself -- alignJVM 212, lawsJVM 86, both
green. So a12fdde alone does not break any law. The open question is only a12fdde COMBINED WITH your
change, which is exactly what your rebase measures and what no amount of my reasoning can settle.

AND THE ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT: scout's exception was justified by PROVEN UNREACHABILITY, not by
"the delta looks small". Yours is reachable. Same rule, same evidence standard, opposite answers --
which is what a rule is for.
